ended: Lost the East 1st Round 2-4 to NY

archetype.name: Early Playoff Exit (defense-first turnaround)
archetype.definition: A 46-36 division winner that rebuilt itself around a top-10 defense and a breakout wing core, then won two one-point games against New York before being blown out three straight times in the first round.

report.headline: A real defense and a division title, then New York ran Atlanta off

recap.finish: 46-36, first in the Southeast; lost the East 1st Round 2-4 to NY
recap.body:
This was the season Atlanta changed what kind of team it is. Across the five prior years in the sheet, the Hawks were an offense-first group whose defense ranked 21st, 26th, 22nd, 27th and 19th. This year the defense ranked 9th, with a 113.7 defensive rating against a league average of 115.7, while the offense slid to the middle at 14th. The 46-36 record was the best of any season on file, good enough to edge Orlando's 45-37 for the Southeast, and it was earned honestly: a +198 point differential implies 47 wins, so the W vs Pt Diff of -1 says no close-game luck propped it up.

The path there was anything but steady. A 10-5 November had them at 13-8, then December fell apart, a 3-11 month in which they allowed 125.43 points a game, the 7-game losing streak presumably sitting somewhere in that collapse. They were still under .500 at 30-31 at the end of February. March flipped the season: 13-2, an 11-game winning streak, and just 110.47 points allowed a game. The finish was a mild cool-off, 6-4 over the last ten with a +6.4 differential a game, though it closed with a 143-117 loss at Miami.

The engine was a perimeter trio. Jalen Johnson made the All-Star team and All-NBA Third Team, leading the roster with 7.5 Win Shares and a 4.2 BPM while handling 566 assists from the wing. Nickeil Alexander-Walker won Most Improved Player on 1,624 points, 251 threes and a 61 TS %. Dyson Daniels did the defensive work, an All-Defensive Second Team guard whose 11.2 On-Off was the best on the roster. Shooting carried the offense (3P % ranked 5th) and the defense lived on forcing mistakes, with Opp TOV % 6th. Opponents' shooting guards had one of the worst nights in the league against them, scoring 25.9 a game, ranked 2nd fewest.

The holes were inside and at the line. The frontcourt graded C-; Onyeka Okongwu was solid with 6 Win Shares and 144 threes from the center spot, but behind him the bigs rated well down their tab. Atlanta ranked 27th in FT Rate, 20th in ORB % and 19th in REB %, so it relied on making jumpers more than creating extra possessions. Small forwards also hurt it: opponents' SFs scored 25.21 a game, 29th in the league, and 1.7 over their own averages.

The playoffs exposed all of it. After losing Game 1 at New York, Atlanta stole Games 2 and 3 by a point apiece, 107-106 and 109-108, and held a 2-1 lead. Then it lost by 16 at home, by 29 at the Garden, and was routed 140-89 at home in Game 6. The postseason Net Rtg of -18.1 ranked 15th of 16, opponents shot a 56.9 eFG %, worst among playoff teams, and Atlanta's 36.8 rebounds a game were also last. Alexander-Walker's TS % dropped to 52.8, Johnson's On-Off sank to -11.2, and CJ McCollum took on a 30.2 USG % without the efficiency to match. Only Okongwu, at a 70.4 TS %, rose to it.

highlights.title: The defense finally showed up
highlights.body: After years of bottom-third defenses, Atlanta ranked 9th with a 113.7 rating, two points better than the league. Turnovers drove it, with Opp TOV % 6th, and Daniels' perimeter work showed up both in his On-Off and in how little opposing shooting guards scored. It came with a core that should return, so it looks more structural than fluky, though the playoff collapse tempers that.

highlights.title: Johnson and Alexander-Walker broke out
highlights.body: Johnson played like an All-NBA wing, leading the team in Win Shares and BPM, and Alexander-Walker's Most Improved season gave Atlanta a second volume shooter at a 61 TS %. Together they are why the 3P % ranked 5th. Both stepped back in the playoffs, but their regular seasons give the next roster a real top end.

highlights.title: A March surge saved the season
highlights.body: At 30-31 through February, Atlanta went 13-2 in March, including an 11-game winning streak, and allowed only 110.47 a game. That month turned a sub-.500 team into a division winner, and the full-season differential backs up the record.

lowlights.title: Three straight blowouts ended it
lowlights.body: Up 2-1 on New York on two one-point wins, Atlanta lost the next three, the last 140-89 at home. Its postseason Net Rtg was 15th of 16 and its opponents' eFG % the worst any playoff defense allowed, so the regular season's defensive gains did not hold up against a better opponent.

lowlights.title: A soft frontcourt and little at the rim
lowlights.body: The frontcourt graded C-, and the team ranked 27th in FT Rate and 20th in ORB %, so the offense depended on jump shots without free points behind them. In the playoffs that became last in rebounds a game among the 16 teams. It is the clearest roster gap the numbers leave.

lowlights.title: The December collapse
lowlights.body: A 3-11 December, with 125.43 points allowed a game, dropped a 13-8 team under .500 and kept it there into March. The defense that ranked 9th overall had a month of looking like the old Hawks, so the swings are worth watching.

arc.note: A strong November gave way to a 3-11 December and a sub-.500 team through February, before a 13-2 March and an 11-game streak carried Atlanta to the division title and a first-round loss.

recap.nextYear: The foundation is the perimeter: Johnson, Alexander-Walker and Daniels produced the bulk of the team's value and the defensive identity, and the record was backed by the margin rather than close-game luck, so 46 wins was a fair reflection of this group. The work is up front. A C- frontcourt, poor free-throw generation and below-average offensive rebounding were tolerable in the regular season and fatal against New York, where Atlanta was outrebounded and out-shot badly. Depth on the wing is also a question, with Risacher and Kispert both carrying negative BPM and On-Off numbers. The playoff blowouts are a small sample, but they point at the same weaknesses the season's numbers did.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season plus a six-game series; playoff sample is small but consistent with season weaknesses.
